concept.name: Limit-if-touched order
concept.definition: A conditional order that becomes a limit order at a specified limit price once a trigger ('touch') price is reached. It combines the trigger logic of a market-if-touched order with the price protection of a limit order.
concept.intuition: It is a standing instruction: 'if the market trades down to my trigger, work a limit order at my chosen price' - you get price control, at the cost of possibly not being filled.
concept.mechanics: The order is held by the broker or venue until the touch price trades; it is then submitted as a limit order at the preset limit price (for a sell LIT the limit is typically at or below the trigger, for a buy LIT at or above it). If the market moves away through the limit, the order rests unfilled.
concept.failure_modes: If the market gaps through both the trigger and the limit price, the order triggers but never fills, leaving the intended entry or exit unexecuted exactly when it was most wanted.
concept.misconceptions: A LIT is not assured of execution once triggered - the limit price can prevent the fill. It is also not identical to a stop-limit order, whose trigger placement convention is the opposite (buy above / sell below the market).
concept.example: Stock trades at $50; you place a buy LIT with trigger $48 and limit $48.10. When $48 trades, a limit order to buy at $48.10 goes live and fills only at $48.10 or better.
